start.text: Report sent. One address typed code into the login form, and the database answered with everything.
start.name: Joshua

A.text: Good work, Joshua. Remember: typed text is data. It only becomes a problem when the site treats it as an order.
A.name: Carla

B.text: So tonight you read each web request as it arrives.
B.name: Carla

C1.text: No. Ciaran O'Brien types one in his name every day. The [b][color=green]rulebook[/color][/b] says look at the whole text, not at one character.
C1.name: Carla

C2.text: No. Names have apostrophes, and searches have spaces. We check what is typed, not how it looks. And our own scanner types code on purpose.
C2.name: Carla

D.text: [b][color=red]Report[/color][/b] the code. Let the rest [b][color=green]pass[/color][/b], even the ones that look odd.
D.name: Carla

E.text: One request at a time. Read what was typed, and what came back.
E.name: Joshua
